title: Validate a square row-major buffer before summing
prompt: Return the long long sum of a flat square matrix with side width. width=0 requires empty data. Reject any size mismatch with invalid_argument without multiplying width*width, which may overflow. Tests use at most 10000 values; their sum fits long long.
signature: long long matrixSum(const std::vector<int>& data,std::size_t width)
driver: int main(){std::size_t w;if(!(std::cin>>w))return 2;std::vector<int> v;int x;while(std::cin>>x)v.push_back(x);try{std::cout<<matrixSum(v,w)<<"\n";}catch(const std::invalid_argument&){std::cout<<"shape mismatch\n";}}

tests.label: Missing element
tests.hint: A partial row is not a square.

tests.label: Huge width
tests.hint: Use division and remainder, not unchecked multiplication.

tests.label: Negative sum
tests.hint: Do not use an unsigned accumulator.

tests.label: Data with zero width
tests.hint: A zero-side matrix contains no elements.

hints: After ruling out width==0, divide the actual size by width.
Only index rows after validating the entire shape.
explanation: For a valid square, row*width+col is within the actual buffer. Checking quotient and remainder avoids computing a potentially overflowing square. The starter silently sums malformed input and outputs 6 for the sample instead of shape mismatch. A plain accumulate is simpler if callers already establish shape; this boundary owns validation. Row-major traversal is a layout choice, not a promised measured speedup.
